project: meet.labattsimon.com — Cal-ID fork: booking-page redesign, calendar reconnect, and location-aware scheduling

items.title: Create the roadmap page
items.summary: A build-status page at /roadmap backed by a single JSON file, so there is one honest record of what was asked for, what is in flight, and what actually happened.
items.notes: Served from public/ as plain HTML rather than as a Next route, so editing the JSON needs no rebuild and the page survives the framework. Zero dependencies — no fetch library, no framework, no CDN. Single id space by construction: 'future' is a status, not a separate array, which is the collision this design exists to avoid.

items.title: Reconnect a calendar whose OAuth grant was revoked
items.summary: Adds a Reconnect action to the credential menu that re-runs OAuth and repairs the existing credential in place, instead of forcing remove-and-re-add.
items.notes: The trigger was a real outage: Google Calendar stopped syncing and the UI said 'try reconnecting' while offering only 'Remove app'. Root cause was not the missing button — the OAuth consent screen was still in Testing, where Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days. Logs showed invalid_grant starting exactly 7 days after connecting. Keeping the credential id matters because DestinationCalendar, SelectedCalendar and event-type metadata all reference it. The credential id travels in OAuth state, which the client composes, so the write is scoped by userId and appId and raises P2025 rather than trusting it.

items.title: Broadsheet theme for the month-view booking page
items.summary: Restyles the public booking page as newsprint: display serif for headline and month, tight grotesk for numerals and controls, duration promoted to a full-width band.
items.notes: Duration moved out of the sidebar because it decides which slots exist, so it has to be read before a date is picked. The serif silently never rendered at first: layout.tsx stripped the quotes next/font emits, and 'Source Serif 4' unquoted is an invalid CSS family because 4 is not a valid identifier, so the whole declaration was dropped and the page fell back to Times. Inter Tight survived the same treatment only because it has no digits — which is exactly why it failed quietly. Took five debugging passes ending in CDP getMatchedStylesForNode to find.

items.title: Make the DURATION label readable
items.summary: The duration label inherited the generic kicker treatment and failed WCAG AA against the band it sits on.
items.notes: Measured ~4:1, below the 4.5 floor for small text. Deliberately not fixed by raising the shared --bs-ink-faint token: that token also greys out unavailable day numbers, where low contrast is carrying meaning, and brightening it globally would make disabled days read as bookable. Ended at 14.98:1 dark / 15.86:1 light.

items.title: Schedule location rules — schema, resolution, API
items.summary: Records where the organiser physically is on given dates, so a booking can resolve to the right location automatically.
items.notes: Two design reversals worth keeping. First: the rules were going on the event type until it became clear they describe a person's whereabouts, not one event type's policy — at event-type scope every new event type needs its own copy of a weekly-changing travel calendar. Second: ordering was dropped as YAGNI on a promise of disjoint day sets, then reinstated once time windows and catch-all rules made overlap unavoidable. Resolution is a pure function evaluated in the schedule's timezone: a Friday 10:00 slot in New York is already Saturday in Sydney. Two traps found: Prisma returns @db.Time pinned to 1970-01-01 UTC so the wall clock lives in the UTC accessors, and @db.Date compared after a zone conversion rolls back a day for anywhere west of Greenwich.

items.title: Schedule location editor
items.summary: Set a default location on each weekday row beside its hours, with a lock toggle, plus a month calendar for overriding specific dates.
items.notes: Built backwards on the first attempt. 'Some weeks Mon/Tue/Wed, others Wed/Thu/Fri' was read as meaning no weekly pattern was worth a default, so only dated assignment was built and the recurring editor was deferred. It actually meant defaults plus freedom to depart from them — which is what the date/days split in the model was for. Second bug: the card was rendered as a sibling of AvailabilitySettings, which returns the whole page Shell, so it appeared underneath the left nav. Neither tsc nor the build catches that — it is valid React rendering in the wrong place. Fixed with a footerSlot, and the weekday control threaded as a slot matching the CopyButton element ScheduleDay already accepts.

items.title: Maintenance page on server errors
items.summary: A 5xx now renders a friendly maintenance page with an unwell-calendar mascot instead of an error name and a block of exception text.
items.notes: Gated to 5xx only: pages/_error shares this component and can pass a 404, which is not an outage and should not claim to be one. The mascot is inline SVG using currentColor, because this renders on the error path where whatever would serve an image may be the thing that just failed. Rendered it before shipping and caught two things that would have gone out blind: the eyes curved upward and read as happy, fighting the entire message, and the thermometer bulb overlapped a leg so it looked like the calendar was stabbing its own shin.

items.title: Fork to labatt/cal-id and push
items.summary: Fork the upstream repo, commit the outstanding work, and push 21 commits that existed only on the server's disk.
items.notes: Caught a leak on the way out. logs/ was untracked but not gitignored and contained the owner's email address 179 times plus OAuth failures and calendar IDs — on a public fork that is world-readable and effectively permanent. Also ignored .next.known-good/, .superpowers/, .playwright-mcp/ and screenshots. Verified gh.env, ecosystem.config.js and seed-google-apps.ts carry no hardcoded secrets. Flagged before forking that a fork of a public repo is permanently public and cannot be converted; the owner chose public anyway.

items.title: Document the fork and how to deploy it
items.summary: README section describing every difference from upstream, plus a from-scratch deployment guide for a new server.
items.notes: The Google section already said 'click PUBLISH APP' but buried it at the end with no reason attached, so it read as optional — which is how the 7-day token expiry in item 2 happened. It now states the consequence, that publishing changes token lifetime rather than access control, and what 'unverified' actually costs. Deployment guide uses the versions this actually runs on rather than generic ones, and documents the $connection_upgrade nginx map and why build.sh exists instead of a bare yarn build.

items.title: Event-type opt-in toggle for schedule locations
items.summary: A control on the event type to turn on useScheduleLocations, plus a warning when a schedule location is missing from that event type's own locations.
items.notes: This is the gate on everything else in this section: the column existed and defaulted to false with no way to set it, so a finished resolution path would still have changed nothing. Scoped to the main schedule only — the restriction schedule governs when a host can be booked, not where they are, so a location toggle there would mean nothing. Persistence came free because the update handler spreads ...rest into the Prisma update. Surprise worth recording: making useScheduleLocations required on FormValues produced zero compiler errors, so the form is assembled from a source that structurally carries every EventType column — adding event-type fields here is cheaper than it looks. NOT FULLY VERIFIED: the toggle renders and both strings are in the shipped client and server bundles, and tsc and the production build are clean, but the click-to-persist loop needs an authenticated session, which cannot be driven from here. Left as working until a human confirms the toggle sticks after a save and reload. CONFIRMED SAVING: the column reads true in the database after a save, so the write path was always correct — the apparent revert was item 14's read-path bug.

items.title: Resolve location in the booking flow
items.summary: Make the booker use the resolved location: set it as the default or lock it outright, and enforce that server-side.
items.notes: The rule must set the value, not merely filter the options. hideWhenJustOneOption only marks the field hidden and never populates it, and an empty responses.location falls through to the default conferencing app — which can end at Cal Video. Filtering alone would silently book the wrong location. Server-side enforcement is required separately: the endpoint accepts whatever is posted, so a crafted request could book in person on a locked day. FOUND WHILE STARTING: the event type on this instance has scheduleId NULL and runs off the owner's defaultScheduleId (1). getPublicEvent selects the schedule relation directly, so that relation is null here and naive plumbing would resolve no rules at all — code that looks correct and silently does nothing in the one configuration that actually exists. Resolution has to use the effective schedule, eventType.scheduleId ?? owner.defaultScheduleId, everywhere, including the server-side check. BUILT AND PARTLY VERIFIED: the public endpoint was called against the live instance and returns the right answer — America/New_York, TPA resolved to inPerson, ZOOM resolved to integrations:zoom, all four rules, Friday locked — with no addresses or credential ids in the payload. The effective-schedule fallback fired for real, since this event type has no schedule of its own. STILL UNVERIFIED: nobody has actually placed a booking. Whether a Friday submission produces a Zoom link and the right location on the confirmation runs through EventManager and the Zoom credential, which cannot be exercised without completing a real booking. Booker behaviour since verified by driving the live page on a mobile viewport, not by inference: Friday locked to Zoom, Tuesday defaulting to the Tampa office and still changeable.

items.title: Location markers on the booking page
items.summary: Show which days are which location before a booker commits to a slot — short code on the day cell, per-slot codes on mixed days, and a legend.
items.notes: Design settled by mockup. Marking only the exception rather than every day: it drops a month from 15 marks to 3, and changes the encoding from hue to presence, which survives greyscale and colour blindness. The first version used two coloured dots, which spent the page's second accent a dozen times a month when the whole point of that accent is that it appears once — and left colour as the only signal. SHIPPED AND SEEN: codes render on the right days — TPA on Tue-Thu, ZOOM on Fri — with a legend beneath, verified by screenshot rather than by reading the diff. Each cell is converted into the schedule's timezone before resolving, so the grid marks the organiser's days rather than the booker's. Days whose morning and afternoon differ show ·· instead of a misleading single code. Also fixed a collision the measurements implied but could not be observed: today's dot sits at top-1/2 plus 8px and the badge at bottom-2px, which overlap in a phone-sized cell whenever today is bookable. Today happened to be unbookable, so no screenshot could show it; the dot is now lifted only when a badge is present.

items.title: Put active sub-projects at the top of the roadmap
items.summary: A section with unfinished work should lead the page; only once all its items are done does it fall below the status tables.
items.notes: The first cut followed the brief literally — sections rendered after every status table — and the result was that all live work sat below nine finished items, which is the opposite of what the brief's own justification asked for ('a section earns the top of the page while its work is live'). Observed it on the rendered page and should have raised it then rather than shipping and waiting to be told. Verified in a browser rather than by reading the diff: heading order is now 'Location-aware bookings → Being worked on → Finished', with no page errors. A section drops back below the status tables automatically once every item in it is done, so nothing has to be remembered when it lands.

items.title: Event type toggle did not survive a reload
items.summary: useScheduleLocations saved correctly but the edit form always rendered it off, so it looked like the setting would not stick.
items.notes: Reported as 'saves then reverts', which reads like a broken write. It was the opposite: the column was already true in the database, so the write was fine and the read was wrong. findById and findByIdForOrgAdmin enumerate every form field explicitly and the new column was not among them, so the form initialised it to false on every load. Adding a column to the schema is not enough — these two selects have to list it as well, which is worth knowing before items 11 and 12 add more. Fix is deployed; confirm by toggling, saving and reloading.

items.title: Warn about locations no event type offers
items.summary: The card now names any schedule location that no opted-in event type can match, and refuses to create an in-person location without an address.
items.notes: Written because both of the first two real locations were unusable and nothing said so. One was typed inPerson but meant Zoom — the type select defaults to In person and it is easy to leave. The other carried an empty-string address, which is not null, so matchScheduleLocation took the address branch and compared "" against the real address and failed. Empty now normalises to null at the source. Also nearly shipped this as useQuery when getEventTypesFromGroup is cursor-paginated and every other call site uses useInfiniteQuery; caught by checking the other usages rather than assuming.

items.title: Locked location showed nothing at all on the booking page
items.summary: Picking a Friday left the booker with no location displayed anywhere, rather than showing Zoom.
items.notes: Self-inflicted and predictable. The location field carries hideWhenJustOneOption, and the responses schema does hidden = hidden || numOptions <= 1, so narrowing a locked day to a single option hides the field completely. The value was still set, so the booking would have come out as Zoom — the booker simply never saw it. I had read that exact flag while deciding the value must be set rather than defaulted, and then filtered to one option anyway. Reported from mobile, but it is not mobile-specific. Fixed by making the field read-only instead of narrowing its options, so it renders with the value set but unchangeable. Driving the real page then exposed a second bug nobody had reported: unlocked days never applied their default at all. The form pre-selects the first configured location, which happened to be Zoom, and a pre-filled value is indistinguishable from a booker's choice — so the "only if empty" guard skipped every time. Now applied once per slot, so changing day re-applies that day's location while a later manual change survives. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER: Friday resolves to integrations:zoom with every radio disabled; Tuesday resolves to inPerson and stays editable.

items.title: Make the picked location obvious, and locked ones obviously deliberate
items.summary: On the details form the selected location barely differs from the unselected ones, and a disabled option looks broken rather than intentionally fixed.
items.notes: Reported after the read-only fix landed. Making the field read-only solved 'no location shown' but created a subtler problem: a greyed-out radio group reads as a bug or a loading state, not as the host having fixed the location on purpose. Being unable to choose has to look deliberate, and the choice that was made has to be legible at a glance. Shipped alongside the markers; the selected row now carries a border, background and weight rather than only a radio dot, and a locked field explains itself in words instead of appearing broken.

items.title: Separate day-cell codes for phone and larger screens
items.summary: Show a fuller code such as ZOOM where there is room, and a two-character one such as ZM on a phone.
items.affects: packages/prisma/schema.prisma, ScheduleLocation editor, public endpoint, day cell
items.notes: Cannot be derived: truncating ZOOM to two characters gives ZO, not ZM, so the short form has to be author-supplied. Stored as a nullable column defaulting to the first two characters of the main code, so existing locations keep working untouched and only a location whose abbreviation is unobvious needs a value typed. VERIFIED: 390px renders TP/ZO and 900px renders TPA/ZOOM, switched by CSS breakpoint rather than by measuring in JavaScript. Worth recording that ZOOM did in fact fit even at 320px — 33px of badge in a 37px cell — so this was legibility rather than overflow.
